Ornament

/OR-nuh-ment/ · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Ornament means an object or feature added to something to make it more attractive; a decoration.

The old theater's ceiling is crowded with plaster ornaments — rosettes, vines, and gilded leaves added purely to delight the eye.

Worked Example

The blacksmith welded a curling iron leaf onto the garden gate — not for strength, just as an ornament.

The iron leaf does no structural work at all; its only job is to make the gate more beautiful. Anything added purely for looks — never for function — is an ornament.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

decoration: Decoration is the broadest word for anything added to make a thing prettier — from birthday streamers to gold leaf — and it can name the whole prettifying scheme. An ornament is one distinct decorative object, added purely to please the eye. Decorations may blanket a room; each carved rosette is an ornament.

adornment: An adornment is a decorative touch that beautifies something, and the word leans toward what is worn or draped — jewels, garlands, embroidery. An ornament is a free-standing decorative object in its own right, often part of a building or display. A necklace is an adornment; the carved rosette above a door is an ornament.

trinket: A trinket is a small, showy object of little practical value — the kind of thing collected on a shelf or won at a fair. An ornament can be finely made and genuinely treasured; what defines it is being added purely for beauty. A trinket is cheap by definition; an ornament need not be.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

eyesore: something ugly and unpleasant to look at

blemish: a mark or flaw that spoils an appearance

Where it sits · how prominent the decoration is — accent → ornament → showpiece

accent vs. ornament: An accent is just a small decorative touch; an ornament is a full decorative object in its own right.

showpiece vs. ornament: A showpiece goes beyond an ornament — it's the star attraction, meant to impress everyone who enters the room.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — orna-

Root — orna-: to adorn, equip (from ornare)

Suffix — -ment

Suffix — -ment: result or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Orna- (from ornare, 'to adorn or equip') + -ment ('result of') gives ornament — 'the result of adorning': an object whose entire purpose is to beautify. No prefix here; the root itself carries the decorating.

Use the root in a new word: ornate

Use the root in a new word: ornate: The ornate mirror frame was carved with roses, ribbons, and tiny gilded birds.

Root Check

Word Choice

Neutral / descriptive

An ornament is added and non-functional — take it away and the object still works, it just looks plainer. The most familiar everyday use is holiday tree ornaments, but architecture, jewelry, and writing can all carry ornament too. The adjective is 'ornamental' ('a purely ornamental balcony').
